subject: QuillCommerce renewal + staged commit uplift — Ops roadmap and pricing
messages:
From: Ben Carter <ben@redwood.com>
To: Sara Liu <sara@quillcommerce.com>
Cc: laura.bennett@redwood.com
Date: Tue, 12 May 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: QuillCommerce renewal + staged commit uplift — Ops roadmap and pricing

Hi Sara,

Great talking yesterday — thanks for walking me through the seasonal forecast and the planned promotions for Q3. Based on the traffic profile you shared and your historical burst patterns, we recommend moving from your current hosted monthly commit (450M tokens) to a phased uplift that lands at 900M/month by month 4.

High level proposal:
- Months 1–2: 600M/month (buffer for promo ramp)
- Months 3–4: 900M/month (standardized commit)
- Soft-burst pocket: +20% for short-term spikes (pre-agreed days)

Operational considerations:
- We can preserve your current rate limits per API key but raise the commit cap; if you prefer higher per-minute throughput we can add a rate band upgrade (recommended for heavy concurrent inference).
- We'll include an SLA amendment for the committed throughput and faster failover to a regional fallback model during sustained outages.

Attached: QuillCommerce_commit_proposal_20260512.pdf and SLA_Amendment_Draft_20260512.pdf (stubs).

Pricing summary (illustrative):
- Effective committed rate for months 1–2: $0.028/1k tokens
- Months 3–4 onward (900M): $0.023/1k tokens
- One-time setup/provisioning credit: $4,500 (applied at signing)

If this looks directionally correct I can pull in pricing/legal for a short amendment and loop in Karthik for final terms support. Would you like us to draft a DocuSign-ready amendment and a phased ops runbook for your SREs?

Best,

Ben Carter
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
ben@redwood.com | +1 415-555-0123

--

Hi Sara — looping procurement in and thanks for the clarity. Actioning items below and attaching the concise artifacts you requested.

What we prepared (attached):
- One-page pricing summary with committed vs burst line items (see QuillCommerce_commit_proposal_20260512.pdf)
- 2-page Operations Runbook (internal) describing ramp steps, keys to monitor, and recommended pre-promo validation checks
- Draft SLA Amendment that adds the throughput SLO, audit log retention (90 days by default for hosted; 365 days available as an add-on), and incident escalation paths.

Responses inline:
- Committed vs burst: pricing sheet separates the committed unit price and the burst overage rate (burst applied only when usage exceeds committed tokens in the month).
- Audit logs: hosted plan includes 90-day retention. For 365-day retention we offer an add-on; we can include it in the amendment as "Audit Log Retention +365" for an additional fixed monthly fee.
- Rate limits: per-key minute-level rate limits remain unchanged by default. We suggest the rate-band add-on if they expect heavy concurrency; otherwise the commit increase plus our autoscaling should absorb most burst traffic.

Commercial:
- If QuillCommerce signs a 12-month amendment with the 900M target, we can extend the effective unit price to $0.021/1k tokens and apply the one-time $4,500 provisioning credit. If they prefer a 6-month agreement we hold the $0.023/1k tokens band and the same provisioning credit.

Next steps:
1) Ben to send DocuSign with two signable items (commit amendment + SLA addendum) — I will include the optional audit-log add-on as an opt-in checkbox.
2) Quill to confirm whether they want the rate-band upgrade.
3) Once signed, our onboarding team will schedule a 60-minute ops walk-through with Quill SREs.

I will attach the pricing + SLA + runbook to the DocuSign packet so procurement has everything in one place. Any edits Karthik recommends for the runbook, flag them back and I'll incorporate before sending.

Best,

Ben Carter
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
